bull.b: The Cohort C result provides clinical support for TSC-101’s ability to achieve the intended transplantation outcome, while the favorable safety profile reduces a key development concern. Reproducible efficacy and safety could support later-stage partnering and preserve value in the hematology platform.

Prioritizing in vivo solid-tumor candidates gives TScan a defined development focus around PRAME and MAGE-A4 rather than spreading resources across a broader portfolio. Advancing both into IND-enabling studies creates concrete regulatory milestones and may improve the platform’s partnership appeal if execution continues.

Projected savings and a runway extending into late 2027 give management more time to advance selected programs and seek partners, reducing immediate financing pressure. This does not establish commercial success, but greater cash duration can support disciplined development and preserve optionality over the next several quarters.

bear.b: Revenue contraction alongside very large operating and net losses shows that the current model has not yet produced a self-sustaining financial base. Continued losses can consume resources needed for clinical development and make future progress dependent on external funding, partnerships, or successful commercialization.

Persistently negative operating and free cash flow indicates ongoing cash burn rather than internally funded growth. At the same time, higher debt relative to equity and declining assets reduce financial flexibility, making it harder to absorb trial setbacks or fund multiple programs without additional capital.

Amgen’s termination removes a significant potential source of collaboration economics: TScan does not expect further milestone or royalty payments tied to the deal, while more than $500 million of potential success-based milestones is lost. This weakens revenue visibility and the partnership-driven model.
